'''Shinkai Sansha Shrine''' (also simply called " '''Shinkai Shrine''' ") is {{ill|Shinto shrine|a shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Miyashiro|en}} , {{ill|10=ja|11=田口村_(長野県)|Taguchi|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久市|Saku, Nagano|en|4=fr|5=Saku (Japon)}}. It was a former prefectural shrine and {{ill|Sōja shrine|the main shrine|en}} of {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久郡|Saku District, Shinano|lt=Saku District|en}} . The {{ill|10=ja|11=deity|enshrined deities|en}} are {{ill|10=ja|11=意岐萩命|Okihagi no Mikoto|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=タケミナカタ|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata no Mikoto|en}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|lt=Kotoshironushi no Mikoto|en}}, and {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Homudawake no Mikoto|en}} . {{ill|10=ja|11=家紋|Mon (emblem)|lt=The sacred crest|en|4=fr|5=Mon (héraldique)}} is {{ill|10=ja|11=梶葉|the Kaji leaf|en}} . The founding date is unknown.
== Overview == The main enshrined deity, {{ill|10=ja|11=興波岐命|Okihagi|lt=Okihagi-no-Mikoto|en}}, is the grandson of the Great God [[Ōkuninushi]] from [[Izumo-taisha]] and the god of development in Saku. Okihagi-no-Mikoto's father is {{ill|10=ja|11=タケミナカタ|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto|en}} from [[Suwa Taisha]], and his mother is {{ill|10=ja|11=上野貫前女神|Ueno Nukisaki no Megami|en}} ({{ill|10=ja|11=荒船大明神|Arafune Daimyojin|en}}). Within the shrine grounds and nearby, there's a group of ancient Kofuns known as the "Forty-Eight Tombs," which some believe are remnants of ancient religious practices. The Shinkai Sansha Shrine, which was considered a "Prefectural Shrine" (Ken-sha) during the [[Kofun period]], came under the influence of Suwa gods during the samurai era and had a powerful domain stretching from Saku to Ueda. Additionally, Shinkai Sansha Shrine is also known as Saku Shrine or Kai Shrine, with the latter name originating from Okihagi-no-Mikoto being the ancestral god of Saku's development. The "{{ill|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|En}}" from the [[Nanboku-chō period]] introduces it as "Nīzaku-no-Kami."
During the Sengoku period, Takeda Shingen prayed for victory and donated a sword, reportedly restoring the shrine's buildings, and the prayer certificate still remains.<ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> In the Edo period, a debate arose over which shrine should be considered the primary one in Saku since Shinkai Sansha Shrine wasn't included among the recognized sites, sparking controversy. During the early Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the three-storied pagoda (which was part of the temple complex Shinkaisan Kamiyama Gongan-in Jingūmitsudera) was to be destroyed, but the shrine argued it was not a pagoda but a treasure house, and that was accepted. The pagoda from the Muromachi period still stands on the shrine grounds. Before World War II, the Shinkai Sansha Shrine's grand procession was held, where priests on horseback paraded through the South and North Saku to the Oagata District.<ref>『佐久の神社と信仰』信濃教育出版部、1989年、261頁。</ref>
== Cultural Assets ==
=== Important Cultural Property (nationally designated) ===
* Three-story pagoda - Built in the late Muromachi period (1515). A three-bay, three-story pagoda with a shingled roof. Designated on August 28, 1907 (Meiji 40). <ref name="#1">『神社考』双葉印刷、1984年、全304頁</ref> * East Main Shrine - Built in the late Muromachi period (1467-1572). The one-bay, Nagare-zukuri style shrine has a cypress bark roof. Designated on July 29, 1937. <ref name="#1" /> Enshrining the chief deity, Okinawa no Mikoto
== Temple grounds ==
* {{ill|10=ja|11=絹笠神社|Kinugasa Shrine|en}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=福田稲荷神社|Fukuda Inari Shrine|en}}
In addition, there is a joint hall for 12 eastern and western sub-shrines. Next to the {{ill|Torii|the torii gate|en}} stands the largest tree in the shrine grounds, a large zelkova tree said to be over 1,000 years old. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref>
== Sacred Tree == [[File:Shinkai_Sansha_Jinja_map.png|thumb| The sacred cedar tree and the zelkova tree near the torii gate]] There is a {{ill|Shinboku|There is a sacred|en}} {{ill|10=ja|11=スギ|Cryptomeria|en}} tree about 20 meters in front of the east main hall. Its age is unknown, but as of 1940 it was over 30 metres tall, 12 metres thick at the base, and 8 metres at its diameter. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> When {{ill|10=ja|11=金剛力士|Nio (Buddhism)|lt=the Niomon Gate|en|4=fr|5=Niō}} burned down in the early Meiji period, the fire spread to the base of the temple, and all {{ill|Ujigami|the parishioners|en}} gathered together and spent several days extinguishing the fire. Before the war, when the trunk of the tree began to lean severely, they received guidance from Dr. {{ill|10=ja|11=本多静六|Honda Seiroku|en}}, a doctor of {{ill|10=ja|11=博士（林学）|forestry|en}} and had it reinforced with donations from all the parishioners. <ref name="nagano" />
== Anecdote ==
* The road taken during the divine procession was called "Shinkaido" and {{ill|Shinko-shiki|the divine procession|en}} itself was called " {{ill|10=ja|11=御幸|Miyuki|en}} " <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 北佐久篇』7ページ。</ref> . * Behind the shrine is Yoshiike Pond. Long ago, a monk learned of this pond after hearing a prophecy from a snake. It is said that when a monk ground ink in the water of the pond and wrote Sanskrit characters, the characters were reflected on 36 sheets of paper below, and so the Goshintomi Festival began. It was also said that anyone who saw a Shinto priest wearing a white mask going to fetch water in the middle of the night would suffer misfortune, so villagers would go to bed early. <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 南佐久篇』121ページ。</ref> * {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久市長|Mayor of Saku City|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=柳田清二|Seiji Yanagida|en}}, spoke about the anime film " {{ill|Your Name|Your Name."|en}} Since it has been introduced as a sacred place for the movie, some people visit the area to verify the location or make a pilgrimage there. <ref>[https://twitter.com/Seiji_Ya/status/771939265534132224 【君の名は。『聖地』新海三社神社】]佐久市長柳田清二Twitter, 2016.9.3</ref>

Next to the {{ill|Torii|the torii gate|en}} stands the largest tree in the shrine grounds, a large zelkova tree said to be over 1,000 years old. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref>
== Sacred Tree == [[File:Shinkai_Sansha_Jinja_map.png|thumb| The sacred cedar tree and the zelkova tree near the torii gate]] There is a {{ill|Shinboku|There is a sacred|en}} {{ill|10=ja|11=スギ|Cryptomeria|en}} tree about 20 meters in front of the east main hall. Its age is unknown, but as of 1940 it was over 30 metres tall, 12 metres thick at the base, and 8 metres at its diameter. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> When {{ill|10=ja|11=金剛力士|Nio (Buddhism)|lt=the Niomon Gate|en|4=fr|5=Niō}} burned down in the early Meiji period, the fire spread to the base of the temple, and all {{ill|Ujigami|the parishioners|en}} gathered together and spent several days extinguishing the fire. Before the war, when the trunk of the tree began to lean severely, they received guidance from Dr. {{ill|10=ja|11=本多静六|Honda Seiroku|en}}, a doctor of {{ill|10=ja|11=博士（林学）|forestry|en}} and had it reinforced with donations from all the parishioners. <ref name="nagano" />
== Anecdote ==
* The road taken during the divine procession was called "Shinkaido" and {{ill|Shinko-shiki|the divine procession|en}} itself was called " {{ill|10=ja|11=御幸|Miyuki|en}} " <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 北佐久篇』7ページ。</ref> . * Behind the shrine is Yoshiike Pond. Long ago, a monk learned of this pond after hearing a prophecy from a snake. It is said that when a monk ground ink in the water of the pond and wrote Sanskrit characters, the characters were reflected on 36 sheets of paper below, and so the Goshintomi Festival began. It was also said that anyone who saw a Shinto priest wearing a white mask going to fetch water in the middle of the night would suffer misfortune, so villagers would go to bed early. <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 南佐久篇』121ページ。</ref> * {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久市長|Mayor of Saku City|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=柳田清二|Seiji Yanagida|en}}, spoke about the anime film " {{ill|Your Name|Your Name."|en}} Since it has been introduced as a sacred place for the movie, some people visit the area to verify the location or make a pilgrimage there. <ref>[https://twitter.com/Seiji_Ya/status/771939265534132224 【君の名は。『聖地』新海三社神社】]佐久市長柳田清二Twitter, 2016.9.3</ref>

{{ill|Shinkai Sansha Shrine|ja|新海三社神社}} is a regional {{ill|Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine|en}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shinkaisansya-jinja Shrine|url=https://www.guidoor.jp/en/places/3414|access-date=2023-11-01|website=Guidoor|language=en}}</ref> in {{ill|Minamisaku District, Nagano|en}} {{ill|Kitasaku District, Nagano|en}} {{ill|Chiisagata District, Nagano|en}} It enshrines many kami of the local region.<!-- Content taken from {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|en}} explaining the concept of it -->
It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>
'''Shinkai Sansha Shrine''' (also simply called " '''Shinkai Shrine''' ") is {{ill|Shinto shrine|a shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Miyashiro|en}} , {{ill|10=ja|11=田口村_(長野県)|Taguchi|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久市|Saku, Nagano|en|4=fr|5=Saku (Japon)}}. It was a former prefectural shrine and {{ill|Sōja shrine|the main shrine|en}} of {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久郡|Saku District, Shinano|lt=Saku District|en}} . The {{ill|10=ja|11=deity|enshrined deities|en}} are {{ill|10=ja|11=意岐萩命|Okihagi no Mikoto|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=タケミナカタ|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata no Mikoto|en}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|lt=Kotoshironushi no Mikoto|en}}, and {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Homudawake no Mikoto|en}} . {{ill|10=ja|11=家紋|Mon (emblem)|lt=The sacred crest|en|4=fr|5=Mon (héraldique)}} is {{ill|10=ja|11=梶葉|the Kaji leaf|en}} . The founding date is unknown.
== Overview == The main enshrined deity, {{ill|10=ja|11=興波岐命|Okihagi|lt=Okihagi-no-Mikoto|en}}, is the grandson of the Great God [[Ōkuninushi]] from [[Izumo-taisha]] and the god of development in Saku. Okihagi-no-Mikoto's father is {{ill|10=ja|11=タケミナカタ|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto|en}} from [[Suwa Taisha]], and his mother is {{ill|10=ja|11=上野貫前女神|Ueno Nukisaki no Megami|en}} ({{ill|10=ja|11=荒船大明神|Arafune Daimyojin|en}}). Within the shrine grounds and nearby, there's a group of ancient Kofuns known as the "Forty-Eight Tombs," which some believe are remnants of ancient religious practices. The Shinkai Sansha Shrine, which was considered a "Prefectural Shrine" (Ken-sha) during the [[Kofun period]], came under the influence of Suwa gods during the samurai era and had a powerful domain stretching from Saku to Ueda. Additionally, Shinkai Sansha Shrine is also known as Saku Shrine or Kai Shrine, with the latter name originating from Okihagi-no-Mikoto being the ancestral god of Saku's development. The "{{ill|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|En}}" from the [[Nanboku-chō period]] introduces it as "Nīzaku-no-Kami."
During the Sengoku period, Takeda Shingen prayed for victory and donated a sword, reportedly restoring the shrine's buildings, and the prayer certificate still remains.<ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> In the Edo period, a debate arose over which shrine should be considered the primary one in Saku since Shinkai Sansha Shrine wasn't included among the recognized sites, sparking controversy. During the early Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the three-storied pagoda (which was part of the temple complex Shinkaisan Kamiyama Gongan-in Jingūmitsudera) was to be destroyed, but the shrine argued it was not a pagoda but a treasure house, and that was accepted. The pagoda from the Muromachi period still stands on the shrine grounds. Before World War II, the Shinkai Sansha Shrine's grand procession was held, where priests on horseback paraded through the South and North Saku to the Oagata District.<ref>『佐久の神社と信仰』信濃教育出版部、1989年、261頁。</ref>
== Cultural Assets ==
=== Important Cultural Property (nationally designated) ===
* Three-story pagoda - Built in the late Muromachi period (1515). A three-bay, three-story pagoda with a shingled roof. Designated on August 28, 1907 (Meiji 40). <ref name="#1">『神社考』双葉印刷、1984年、全304頁</ref> * East Main Shrine - Built in the late Muromachi period (1467-1572). The one-bay, Nagare-zukuri style shrine has a cypress bark roof. Designated on July 29, 1937. <ref name="#1" /> Enshrining the chief deity, Okinawa no Mikoto

{{ill|Shinkai Sansha Shrine|ja|新海三社神社}} is a regional {{ill|Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine|en}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shinkaisansya-jinja Shrine|url=https://www.guidoor.jp/en/places/3414|access-date=2023-11-01|website=Guidoor|language=en}}</ref> in {{ill|Minamisaku District, Nagano|en}} {{ill|Kitasaku District, Nagano|en}} {{ill|Chiisagata District, Nagano|en}} It enshrines many kami of the local region.<!-- Content taken from {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|en}} explaining the concept of it -->
It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>
'''Shinkai Sansha Shrine''' (also simply called " '''Shinkai Shrine''' ") is {{ill|Shinto shrine|a shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Miyashiro|en}} , {{ill|10=ja|11=田口村_(長野県)|Taguchi|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久市|Saku, Nagano|en|4=fr|5=Saku (Japon)}}. It was a former prefectural shrine and {{ill|Sōja shrine|the main shrine|en}} of {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久郡|Saku District, Shinano|lt=Saku District|en}} . The {{ill|10=ja|11=deity|enshrined deities|en}} are {{ill|10=ja|11=意岐萩命|Okihagi no Mikoto|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=タケミナカタ|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata no Mikoto|en}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|lt=Kotoshironushi no Mikoto|en}}, and {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Homudawake no Mikoto|en}} . {{ill|10=ja|11=家紋|Mon (emblem)|lt=The sacred crest|en|4=fr|5=Mon (héraldique)}} is {{ill|10=ja|11=梶葉|the Kaji leaf|en}} . The founding date is unknown.
== Overview == The main enshrined deity, {{ill|10=ja|11=興波岐命|Okihagi|lt=Okihagi-no-Mikoto|en}}, is the grandson of the Great God [[Ōkuninushi]] from [[Izumo-taisha]] and the god of development in Saku. Okihagi-no-Mikoto's father is {{ill|10=ja|11=タケミナカタ|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto|en}} from [[Suwa Taisha]], and his mother is {{ill|10=ja|11=上野貫前女神|Ueno Nukisaki no Megami|en}} ({{ill|10=ja|11=荒船大明神|Arafune Daimyojin|en}}). Within the shrine grounds and nearby, there's a group of ancient Kofuns known as the "Forty-Eight Tombs," which some believe are remnants of ancient religious practices. The Shinkai Sansha Shrine, which was considered a "Prefectural Shrine" (Ken-sha) during the [[Kofun period]], came under the influence of Suwa gods during the samurai era and had a powerful domain stretching from Saku to Ueda. Additionally, Shinkai Sansha Shrine is also known as Saku Shrine or Kai Shrine, with the latter name originating from Okihagi-no-Mikoto being the ancestral god of Saku's development. The "{{ill|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|En}}" from the [[Nanboku-chō period]] introduces it as "Nīzaku-no-Kami."
During the Sengoku period, Takeda Shingen prayed for victory and donated a sword, reportedly restoring the shrine's buildings, and the prayer certificate still remains.<ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> In the Edo period, a debate arose over which shrine should be considered the primary one in Saku since Shinkai Sansha Shrine wasn't included among the recognized sites, sparking controversy. During the early Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the three-storied pagoda (which was part of the temple complex Shinkaisan Kamiyama Gongan-in Jingūmitsudera) was to be destroyed, but the shrine argued it was not a pagoda but a treasure house, and that was accepted. The pagoda from the Muromachi period still stands on the shrine grounds. Before World War II, the Shinkai Sansha Shrine's grand procession was held, where priests on horseback paraded through the South and North Saku to the Oagata District.<ref>『佐久の神社と信仰』信濃教育出版部、1989年、261頁。</ref>
== Cultural Assets ==
=== Important Cultural Property (nationally designated) ===
* Three-story pagoda - Built in the late Muromachi period (1515). A three-bay, three-story pagoda with a shingled roof. Designated on August 28, 1907 (Meiji 40). <ref name="#1">『神社考』双葉印刷、1984th year 、全304頁</ref> * East Main Shrine - Built in the late Muromachi period (1467-1572). The one-bay, Nagare-zukuri style shrine has a cypress bark roof. Designated on July 29, 1937. <ref name="#1" /> Enshrining the chief deity, Okinawa no Mikoto
== Temple grounds ==
* {{ill|10=ja|11=絹笠神社|Kinugasa Shrine|en}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=福田稲荷神社|Fukuda Inari Shrine|en}}
In addition, there is a joint hall for 12 eastern and western sub-shrines. Next to the {{ill|Torii|the torii gate|en}} stands the largest tree in the shrine grounds, a large zelkova tree said to be over 1,000 years old. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref>
== Sacred Tree == [[File:Shinkai_Sansha_Jinja_map.png|thumb| The sacred cedar tree and the zelkova tree near the torii gate]] There is a {{ill|Shinboku|There is a sacred|en}} {{ill|10=ja|11=スギ|Cryptomeria|en}} tree about 20 meters in front of the east main hall. Its age is unknown, but as of 1940 it was over 30 metres tall, 12 metres thick at the base, and 8 metres at its diameter. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> When {{ill|10=ja|11=金剛力士|Nio (Buddhism)|lt=the Niomon Gate|en|4=fr|5=Niō}} burned down in the early Meiji period, the fire spread to the base of the temple, and all {{ill|Ujigami|the parishioners|en}} gathered together and spent several days extinguishing the fire. Before the war, when the trunk of the tree began to lean severely, they received guidance from Dr. {{ill|10=ja|11=本多静六|Honda Seiroku|en}}, a doctor of {{ill|10=ja|11=博士（林学）|forestry|en}} and had it reinforced with donations from all the parishioners. <ref name="nagano" />

Long ago, a monk learned of this pond after hearing a prophecy from a snake. It is said that when a monk ground ink in the water of the pond and wrote Sanskrit characters, the characters were reflected on 36 sheets of paper below, and so the Goshintomi Festival began. {{ill|Shinkai Sansha Shrine|ja|新海三社神社}} is a regional {{ill|Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine|en}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shinkaisansya-jinja Shrine|url=https://www.guidoor.jp/en/places/3414|access-date=2023-11-01|website=Guidoor|language=en}}</ref> in {{ill|Minamisaku District, Nagano|en}} {{ill|Kitasaku District, Nagano|en}} {{ill|Chiisagata District, Nagano|en}} It enshrines many kami of the local region.<!-- Content taken from {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|en}} explaining the concept of it -->
It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>
'''Shinkai Sansha Shrine''' (also simply called " '''Shinkai Shrine''' ") is {{ill|Shinto shrine|a shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Miyashiro|en}} , {{ill|10=ja|11=田口村_(長野県)|Taguchi|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久市|Saku, Nagano|en|4=fr|5=Saku (Japon)}}. It was a former prefectural shrine and {{ill|Sōja shrine|the main shrine|en}} of {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久郡|Saku District, Shinano|lt=Saku District|en}} . The {{ill|10=ja|11=deity|enshrined deities|en}} are {{ill|10=ja|11=意岐萩命|Okihagi no Mikoto|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=タケミナカタ|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata no Mikoto|en}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|lt=Kotoshironushi no Mikoto|en}}, and {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Homudawake no Mikoto|en}} . {{ill|10=ja|11=家紋|Mon (emblem)|lt=The sacred crest|en|4=fr|5=Mon (héraldique)}} is {{ill|10=ja|11=梶葉|the Kaji leaf|en}} . The founding date is unknown.
== Overview == The main enshrined deity, {{ill|10=ja|11=興波岐命|Okihagi|lt=Okihagi-no-Mikoto|en}}, is the grandson of the Great God [[Ōkuninushi]] from [[Izumo-taisha]] and the god of development in Saku. Okihagi-no-Mikoto's father is {{ill|10=ja|11=タケミナカタ|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto|en}} from [[Suwa Taisha]], and his mother is {{ill|10=ja|11=上野貫前女神|Ueno Nukisaki no Megami|en}} ({{ill|10=ja|11=荒船大明神|Arafune Daimyojin|en}}). Within the shrine grounds and nearby, there's a group of ancient Kofuns known as the "Forty-Eight Tombs," which some believe are remnants of ancient religious practices. The Shinkai Sansha Shrine, which was considered a "Prefectural Shrine" (Ken-sha) during the [[Kofun period]], came under the influence of Suwa gods during the samurai era and had a powerful domain stretching from Saku to Ueda. Additionally, Shinkai Sansha Shrine is also known as Saku Shrine or Kai Shrine, with the latter name originating from Okihagi-no-Mikoto being the ancestral god of Saku's development. The "{{ill|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|En}}" from the [[Nanboku-chō period]] introduces it as "Nīzaku-no-Kami."
During the Sengoku period, Takeda Shingen prayed for victory and donated a sword, reportedly restoring the shrine's buildings, and the prayer certificate still remains.<ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> In the Edo period, a debate arose over which shrine should be considered the primary one in Saku since Shinkai Sansha Shrine wasn't included among the recognized sites, sparking controversy. During the early Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the three-storied pagoda (which was part of the temple complex Shinkaisan Kamiyama Gongan-in Jingūmitsudera) was to be destroyed, but the shrine argued it was not a pagoda but a treasure house, and that was accepted. The pagoda from the Muromachi period still stands on the shrine grounds. Before World War II, the Shinkai Sansha Shrine's grand procession was held, where priests on horseback paraded through the South and North Saku to the Oagata District.<ref>『佐久の神社と信仰』信濃教育出版部、1989th year 、261頁。</ref>
== Cultural Assets ==
=== Important Cultural Property (nationally designated) ===
* Three-story pagoda - Built in the late Muromachi period (1515). A three-bay, three-story pagoda with a shingled roof. Designated on August 28, 1907 (Meiji 40). <ref name="#1">『神社考』双葉印刷、1984th year 、全304頁</ref> * East Main Shrine - Built in the late Muromachi period (1467-1572). The one-bay, Nagare-zukuri style shrine has a cypress bark roof. Designated on July 29, 1937. <ref name="#1" /> Enshrining the chief deity, Okinawa no Mikoto
== Temple grounds ==
* {{ill|10=ja|11=絹笠神社|Kinugasa Shrine|en}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=福田稲荷神社|Fukuda Inari Shrine|en}}
In addition, there is a joint hall for 12 eastern and western sub-shrines. Next to the {{ill|Torii|the torii gate|en}} stands the largest tree in the shrine grounds, a large zelkova tree said to be over 1,000 years old. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref>
== Sacred Tree == [[File:Shinkai_Sansha_Jinja_map.png|thumb| The sacred cedar tree and the zelkova tree near the torii gate]] There is a {{ill|Shinboku|There is a sacred|en}} {{ill|10=ja|11=スギ|Cryptomeria|en}} tree about 20 meters in front of the east main hall. Its age is unknown, but as of 1940 it was over 30 metres tall, 12 metres thick at the base, and 8 metres at its diameter. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> When {{ill|10=ja|11=金剛力士|Nio (Buddhism)|lt=the Niomon Gate|en|4=fr|5=Niō}} burned down in the early Meiji period, the fire spread to the base of the temple, and all {{ill|Ujigami|the parishioners|en}} gathered together and spent several days extinguishing the fire. Before the war, when the trunk of the tree began to lean severely, they received guidance from Dr. {{ill|10=ja|11=本多静六|Honda Seiroku|en}}, a doctor of {{ill|10=ja|11=博士（林学）|forestry|en}} and had it reinforced with donations from all the parishioners. <ref name="nagano" />
== Anecdote ==
* The road taken during the divine procession was called "Shinkaido" and {{ill|Shinko-shiki|the divine procession|en}} itself was called " {{ill|10=ja|11=御幸|Miyuki|en}} " <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 北佐久篇』7ページ。</ref> . * Behind the shrine is Yoshiike Pond. Long ago, a monk learned of this pond after hearing a prophecy from a snake. It is said that when a monk ground ink in the water of the pond and wrote Sanskrit characters, the characters were reflected on 36 sheets of paper below, and so the Goshintomi Festival began. It was also said that anyone who saw a Shinto priest wearing a white mask going to fetch water in the middle of the night would suffer misfortune, so villagers would go to bed early. <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 南佐久篇』121ページ。</ref> * {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久市長|Mayor of Saku City|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=柳田清二|Seiji Yanagida|en}}, spoke about the anime film " {{ill|Your Name|Your Name."|en}} Since it has been introduced as a sacred place for the movie, some people visit the area to verify the location or make a pilgrimage there. <ref>[https://twitter.com/Seiji_Ya/status/771939265534132224 【君の名は。『聖地』新海三社神社】]佐久市長柳田清二Twitter, 2016.9.3</ref>

{{ill|Shinkai Sansha Shrine|ja|新海三社神社}} is a regional {{ill|Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine|en}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shinkaisansya-jinja Shrine|url=https://www.guidoor.jp/en/places/3414|access-date=2023-11-01|website=Guidoor|language=en}}</ref> in {{ill|Minamisaku District, Nagano|en}} {{ill|Kitasaku District, Nagano|en}} {{ill|Chiisagata District, Nagano|en}} It enshrines many kami of the local region.<!-- Content taken from {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|en}} explaining the concept of it -->
It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>
'''Shinkai Sansha Shrine''' (also simply called " '''Shinkai Shrine''' ") is {{ill|Shinto shrine|a shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Miyashiro|en}} , {{ill|10=ja|11=田口村_(長野県)|Taguchi|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久市|Saku, Nagano|en|4=fr|5=Saku (Japon)}}. It was a former prefectural shrine and {{ill|Sōja shrine|the main shrine|en}} of {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久郡|Saku District, Shinano|lt=Saku District|en}} . The {{ill|10=ja|11=deity|enshrined deities|en}} are {{ill|10=ja|11=意岐萩命|Okihagi no Mikoto|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=タケミナカタ|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata no Mikoto|en}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|lt=Kotoshironushi no Mikoto|en}}, and {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Homudawake no Mikoto|en}} . {{ill|10=ja|11=家紋|Mon (emblem)|lt=The sacred crest|en|4=fr|5=Mon (héraldique)}} is {{ill|10=ja|11=梶葉|the Kaji leaf|en}} . The founding date is unknown.
== Overview == The main enshrined deity, {{ill|10=ja|11=興波岐命|Okihagi|lt=Okihagi-no-Mikoto|en}}, is the grandson of the Great God [[Ōkuninushi]] from [[Izumo-taisha]] and the god of development in Saku. Okihagi-no-Mikoto's father is {{ill|10=ja|11=タケミナカタ|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto|en}} from [[Suwa Taisha]], and his mother is {{ill|10=ja|11=上野貫前女神|Ueno Nukisaki no Megami|en}} ({{ill|10=ja|11=荒船大明神|Arafune Daimyojin|en}}). Within the shrine grounds and nearby, there's a group of ancient Kofuns known as the "Forty-Eight Tombs," which some believe are remnants of ancient religious practices. The Shinkai Sansha Shrine, which was considered a "Prefectural Shrine" (Ken-sha) during the [[Kofun period]], came under the influence of Suwa gods during the samurai era and had a powerful domain stretching from Saku to Ueda. Additionally, Shinkai Sansha Shrine is also known as Saku Shrine or Kai Shrine, with the latter name originating from Okihagi-no-Mikoto being the ancestral god of Saku's development. The "{{ill|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|En}}" from the [[Nanboku-chō period]] introduces it as "Nīzaku-no-Kami."
During the Sengoku period, Takeda Shingen prayed for victory and donated a sword, reportedly restoring the shrine's buildings, and the prayer certificate still remains.<ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> In the Edo period, a debate arose over which shrine should be considered the primary one in Saku since Shinkai Sansha Shrine wasn't included among the recognized sites, sparking controversy. During the early Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the three-storied pagoda (which was part of the temple complex Shinkaisan Kamiyama Gongan-in Jingūmitsudera) was to be destroyed, but the shrine argued it was not a pagoda but a treasure house, and that was accepted. The pagoda from the Muromachi period still stands on the shrine grounds. Before World War II, the Shinkai Sansha Shrine's grand procession was held, where priests on horseback paraded through the South and North Saku to the Oagata District.<ref>『佐久の神社と信仰』信濃教育出版部、1989th year 、261頁。</ref>
== Cultural Assets ==
=== Important Cultural Property (nationally designated) ===
* Three-story pagoda - Built in the late Muromachi period (1515). A three-bay, three-story pagoda with a shingled roof. Designated on August 28, 1907 (Meiji 40). <ref name="#1">『神社考』双葉印刷、1984th year 、全304頁</ref> * East Main Shrine - Built in the late Muromachi period (1467-1572). The one-bay, Nagare-zukuri style shrine has a cypress bark roof. Designated on July 29, 1937. <ref name="#1" /> Enshrining the chief deity, Okinawa no Mikoto
== Temple grounds ==
* {{ill|10=ja|11=絹笠神社|Kinugasa Shrine|en}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=福田稲荷神社|Fukuda Inari Shrine|en}}
In addition, there is a joint hall for 12 eastern and western sub-shrines. Next to the {{ill|Torii|the torii gate|en}} stands the largest tree in the shrine grounds, a large zelkova tree said to be over 1,000 years old. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref>
== Sacred Tree == [[File:Shinkai_Sansha_Jinja_map.png|thumb| The sacred cedar tree and the zelkova tree near the torii gate]] There is a {{ill|Shinboku|There is a sacred|en}} {{ill|10=ja|11=スギ|Cryptomeria|en}} tree about 20 meters in front of the east main hall. Its age is unknown, but as of 1940 it was over 30 metres tall, 12 metres thick at the base, and 8 metres at its diameter. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> When {{ill|10=ja|11=金剛力士|Nio (Buddhism)|lt=the Niomon Gate|en|4=fr|5=Niō}} burned down in the early Meiji period, the fire spread to the base of the temple, and all {{ill|Ujigami|the parishioners|en}} gathered together and spent several days extinguishing the fire. Before the war, when the trunk of the tree began to lean severely, they received guidance from Dr. {{ill|10=ja|11=本多静六|Honda Seiroku|en}}, a doctor of {{ill|10=ja|11=博士（林学）|forestry|en}} and had it reinforced with donations from all the parishioners. <ref name="nagano" />
== Anecdote ==
* The road taken during the divine procession was called "Shinkaido" and {{ill|Shinko-shiki|the divine procession|en}} itself was called " {{ill|10=ja|11=御幸|Miyuki|en}} " <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 北佐久篇』7ページ。</ref> . * Behind the shrine is Yoshiike Pond. Long ago, a monk learned of this pond after hearing a prophecy from a snake. It is said that when a monk ground ink in the water of the pond and wrote Sanskrit characters, the characters were reflected on 36 sheets of paper below, and so the Goshintomi Festival began. It was also said that anyone who saw a Shinto priest wearing a white mask going to fetch water in the middle of the night would suffer misfortune, so villagers would go to bed early. <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 南佐久篇』121ページ。</ref> * {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久市長|Mayor of Saku City|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=柳田清二|Seiji Yanagida|en}}, spoke about the anime film " {{ill|Your Name|Your Name."|en}} Since it has been introduced as a sacred place for the movie, some people visit the area to verify the location or make a pilgrimage there. <ref>[https://twitter.com/Seiji_Ya/status/771939265534132224 【君の名は。『聖地』新海三社神社】]佐久市長柳田清二Twitter, 2016.9.3</ref>

{{ill|Shinkai Sansha Shrine|ja|新海三社神社}} is a regional {{ill|Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine|en}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shinkaisansya-jinja Shrine|url=https://www.guidoor.jp/en/places/3414|access-date=2023-11-01|website=Guidoor|language=en}}</ref> in {{ill|Minamisaku District, Nagano|en}} {{ill|Kitasaku District, Nagano|en}} {{ill|Chiisagata District, Nagano|en}} It enshrines many kami of the local region.<!-- Content taken from {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|en}} explaining the concept of it -->
It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>
'''Shinkai Sansha Shrine''' (also simply called " '''Shinkai Shrine''' ") is {{ill|Shinto shrine|a shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Miyashiro|en}} , {{ill|10=ja|11=田口村_(長野県)|Taguchi|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久市|Saku, Nagano|en|4=fr|5=Saku (Japon)}}. It was a former prefectural shrine and {{ill|Sōja shrine|the main shrine|en}} of {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久郡|Saku District, Shinano|lt=Saku District|en}} . The {{ill|10=ja|11=deity|enshrined deities|en}} are {{ill|10=ja|11=意岐萩命|Okihagi no Mikoto|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=タケミナカタ|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata no Mikoto|en}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|lt=Kotoshironushi no Mikoto|en}}, and {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Homudawake no Mikoto|en}} . {{ill|10=ja|11=家紋|Mon (emblem)|lt=The sacred crest|en|4=fr|5=Mon (héraldique)}} is {{ill|10=ja|11=梶葉|the Kaji leaf|en}} . The founding date is unknown.
== Overview == The main enshrined deity, {{ill|10=ja|11=興波岐命|Okihagi|lt=Okihagi-no-Mikoto|en}}, is the grandson of the Great God [[Ōkuninushi]] from [[Izumo-taisha]] and the god of development in Saku. Okihagi-no-Mikoto's father is {{ill|10=ja|11=タケミナカタ|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto|en}} from [[Suwa Taisha]], and his mother is {{ill|10=ja|11=上野貫前女神|Ueno Nukisaki no Megami|en}} ({{ill|10=ja|11=荒船大明神|Arafune Daimyojin|en}}). Within the shrine grounds and nearby, there's a group of ancient Kofuns known as the "Forty-Eight Tombs," which some believe are remnants of ancient religious practices. The Shinkai Sansha Shrine, which was considered a "Prefectural Shrine" (Ken-sha) during the [[Kofun period]], came under the influence of Suwa gods during the samurai era and had a powerful domain stretching from Saku to Ueda. Additionally, Shinkai Sansha Shrine is also known as Saku Shrine or Kai Shrine, with the latter name originating from Okihagi-no-Mikoto being the ancestral god of Saku's development. The "{{ill|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|En}}" from the [[Nanboku-chō period]] introduces it as "Nīzaku-no-Kami."
During the Sengoku period, Takeda Shingen prayed for victory and donated a sword, reportedly restoring the shrine's buildings, and the prayer certificate still remains.<ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> In the Edo period, a debate arose over which shrine should be considered the primary one in Saku since Shinkai Sansha Shrine wasn't included among the recognized sites, sparking controversy. During the early Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the three-storied pagoda (which was part of the temple complex Shinkaisan Kamiyama Gongan-in Jingūmitsudera) was to be destroyed, but the shrine argued it was not a pagoda but a treasure house, and that was accepted. The pagoda from the Muromachi period still stands on the shrine grounds. Before World War II, the Shinkai Sansha Shrine's grand procession was held, where priests on horseback paraded through the South and North Saku to the Oagata District.<ref>『佐久の神社と信仰』信濃教育出版部、1989th year 、261頁。</ref>
== Cultural Assets ==
=== Important Cultural Property (nationally designated) ===
* Three-story pagoda - Built in the late Muromachi period (1515). A three-bay, three-story pagoda with a shingled roof. Designated on August 28, 1907 (Meiji 40). <ref name="#1">『神社考』双葉印刷、1984th year 、全304頁</ref> * East Main Shrine - Built in the late Muromachi period (1467-1572). The one-bay, Nagare-zukuri style shrine has a cypress bark roof. Designated on July 29, 1937. <ref name="#1" /> Enshrining the chief deity, Okinawa no Mikoto
== Temple grounds ==
* {{ill|10=ja|11=絹笠神社|Kinugasa Shrine|en}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=福田稲荷神社|Fukuda Inari Shrine|en}}
In addition, there is a joint hall for 12 eastern and western sub-shrines. Next to the {{ill|Torii|the torii gate|en}} stands the largest tree in the shrine grounds, a large zelkova tree said to be over 1,000 years old. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref>
== Sacred Tree == [[File:Shinkai_Sansha_Jinja_map.png|thumb| The sacred cedar tree and the zelkova tree near the torii gate]] There is a {{ill|Shinboku|There is a sacred|en}} {{ill|10=ja|11=スギ|Cryptomeria|en}} tree about 20 meters in front of the east main hall. Its age is unknown, but as of 1940 it was over 30 metres tall, 12 metres thick at the base, and 8 metres at its diameter. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> When {{ill|10=ja|11=金剛力士|Nio (Buddhism)|lt=the Niomon Gate|en|4=fr|5=Niō}} burned down in the early Meiji period, the fire spread to the base of the temple, and all {{ill|Ujigami|the parishioners|en}} gathered together and spent several days extinguishing the fire. Before the war, when the trunk of the tree began to lean severely, they received guidance from Dr. {{ill|10=ja|11=本多静六|Honda Seiroku|en}}, a doctor of {{ill|10=ja|11=博士（林学）|forestry|en}} and had it reinforced with donations from all the parishioners. <ref name="nagano" />
== Anecdote ==
* The road taken during the divine procession was called "Shinkaido" and {{ill|Shinko-shiki|the divine procession|en}} itself was called " {{ill|10=ja|11=御幸|Miyuki|en}} " <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 北佐久篇』7ページ。</ref> . * Behind the shrine is Yoshiike Pond. Long ago, a monk learned of this pond after hearing a prophecy from a snake. It is said that when a monk ground ink in the water of the pond and wrote Sanskrit characters, the characters were reflected on 36 sheets of paper below, and so the Goshintomi Festival began. It was also said that anyone who saw a Shinto priest wearing a white mask going to fetch water in the middle of the night would suffer misfortune, so villagers would go to bed early. <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 南佐久篇』121ページ。</ref> * {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久市長|Mayor of Saku City|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=柳田清二|Seiji Yanagida|en}}, spoke about the anime film " {{ill|Your Name|Your Name."|en}} Since it has been introduced as a sacred place for the movie, some people visit the area to verify the location or make a pilgrimage there. <ref>[https://twitter.com/Seiji_Ya/status/771939265534132224 【君の名は。『聖地』新海三社神社】]佐久市長柳田清二Twitter, 2016.9.3</ref>

{{ill|Shinkai Sansha Shrine|ja|新海三社神社}} is a regional {{ill|Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine|en}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shinkaisansya-jinja Shrine|url=https://www.guidoor.jp/en/places/3414|access-date=2023-11-01|website=Guidoor|language=en}}</ref> in {{ill|Minamisaku District, Nagano|en}} {{ill|Kitasaku District, Nagano|en}} {{ill|Chiisagata District, Nagano|en}} It enshrines many kami of the local region.<!-- Content taken from {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|en}} explaining the concept of it -->
It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>
'''Shinkai Sansha Shrine''' (also simply called " '''Shinkai Shrine''' ") is {{ill|Shinto shrine|a shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Miyashiro|en}} , {{ill|10=ja|11=田口村_(長野県)|Taguchi|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久市|Saku, Nagano|en|4=fr|5=Saku (Japon)}}. It was a former prefectural shrine and {{ill|Sōja shrine|the main shrine|en}} of {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久郡|Saku District, Shinano|lt=Saku District|en}} . The {{ill|10=ja|11=deity|enshrined deities|en}} are {{ill|10=ja|11=意岐萩命|Okihagi no Mikoto|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=タケミナカタ|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata no Mikoto|en}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|lt=Kotoshironushi no Mikoto|en}}, and {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Homudawake no Mikoto|en}} . {{ill|10=ja|11=家紋|Mon (emblem)|lt=The sacred crest|en|4=fr|5=Mon (héraldique)}} is {{ill|10=ja|11=梶葉|the Kaji leaf|en}} . The founding date is unknown.
== Overview == The main enshrined deity, {{ill|10=ja|11=興波岐命|Okihagi|lt=Okihagi-no-Mikoto|en}}, is the grandson of the Great God [[Ōkuninushi]] from [[Izumo-taisha]] and the god of development in Saku. Okihagi-no-Mikoto's father is {{ill|10=ja|11=タケミナカタ|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto|en}} from [[Suwa Taisha]], and his mother is {{ill|10=ja|11=上野貫前女神|Ueno Nukisaki no Megami|en}} ({{ill|10=ja|11=荒船大明神|Arafune Daimyojin|en}}). Within the shrine grounds and nearby, there's a group of ancient Kofuns known as the "Forty-Eight Tombs," which some believe are remnants of ancient religious practices. The Shinkai Sansha Shrine, which was considered a "Prefectural Shrine" (Ken-sha) during the [[Kofun period]], came under the influence of Suwa gods during the samurai era and had a powerful domain stretching from Saku to Ueda. Additionally, Shinkai Sansha Shrine is also known as Saku Shrine or Kai Shrine, with the latter name originating from Okihagi-no-Mikoto being the ancestral god of Saku's development. The "{{ill|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|En}}" from the [[Nanboku-chō period]] introduces it as "Nīzaku-no-Kami."
During the Sengoku period, Takeda Shingen prayed for victory and donated a sword, reportedly restoring the shrine's buildings, and the prayer certificate still remains.<ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> In the Edo period, a debate arose over which shrine should be considered the primary one in Saku since Shinkai Sansha Shrine wasn't included among the recognized sites, sparking controversy. During the early Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the three-storied pagoda (which was part of the temple complex Shinkaisan Kamiyama Gongan-in Jingūmitsudera) was to be destroyed, but the shrine argued it was not a pagoda but a treasure house, and that was accepted. The pagoda from the Muromachi period still stands on the shrine grounds. Before World War II, the Shinkai Sansha Shrine's grand procession was held, where priests on horseback paraded through the South and North Saku to the Oagata District.<ref>『佐久の神社と信仰』信濃教育出版部、1989th year 、261頁。</ref>
== Cultural Assets ==
=== Important Cultural Property (nationally designated) ===
* Three-story pagoda - Built in the late Muromachi period (1515). A three-bay, three-story pagoda with a shingled roof. Designated on August 28, 1907 (Meiji 40). <ref name="#1">『神社考』双葉印刷、1984th year 、全304頁</ref> * East Main Shrine - Built in the late Muromachi period (1467-1572). The one-bay, Nagare-zukuri style shrine has a cypress bark roof. Designated on July 29, 1937. <ref name="#1" /> Enshrining the chief deity, Okinawa no Mikoto
== Temple grounds ==
* {{ill|10=ja|11=絹笠神社|Kinugasa Shrine|en}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=福田稲荷神社|Fukuda Inari Shrine|en}}
In addition, there is a joint hall for 12 eastern and western sub-shrines. Next to the {{ill|Torii|the torii gate|en}} stands the largest tree in the shrine grounds, a large zelkova tree said to be over 1,000 years old. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref>
== Sacred Tree == [[File:Shinkai_Sansha_Jinja_map.png|thumb| The sacred cedar tree and the zelkova tree near the torii gate]] There is a {{ill|Shinboku|There is a sacred|en}} {{ill|10=ja|11=スギ|Cryptomeria|en}} tree about 20 meters in front of the east main hall. Its age is unknown, but as of 1940 it was over 30 metres tall, 12 metres thick at the base, and 8 metres at its diameter. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> When {{ill|10=ja|11=金剛力士|Nio (Buddhism)|lt=the Niomon Gate|en|4=fr|5=Niō}} burned down in the early Meiji period, the fire spread to the base of the temple, and all {{ill|Ujigami|the parishioners|en}} gathered together and spent several days extinguishing the fire. Before the war, when the trunk of the tree began to lean severely, they received guidance from Dr. {{ill|10=ja|11=本多静六|Honda Seiroku|en}}, a doctor of {{ill|10=ja|11=博士（林学）|forestry|en}} and had it reinforced with donations from all the parishioners. <ref name="nagano" />
== Anecdote ==
* The road taken during the divine procession was called "Shinkaido" and {{ill|Shinko-shiki|the divine procession|en}} itself was called " {{ill|10=ja|11=御幸|Miyuki|en}} " <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 北佐久篇』7ページ。</ref> . * Behind the shrine is Yoshiike Pond. Long ago, a monk learned of this pond after hearing a prophecy from a snake. It is said that when a monk ground ink in the water of the pond and wrote Sanskrit characters, the characters were reflected on 36 sheets of paper below, and so the Goshintomi Festival began. It was also said that anyone who saw a Shinto priest wearing a white mask going to fetch water in the middle of the night would suffer misfortune, so villagers would go to bed early. <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 南佐久篇』121ページ。</ref> * {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久市長|Mayor of Saku City|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=柳田清二|Seiji Yanagida|en}}, spoke about the anime film " {{ill|Your Name|Your Name."|en}} Since it has been introduced as a sacred place for the movie, some people visit the area to verify the location or make a pilgrimage there. <ref>[https://twitter.com/Seiji_Ya/status/771939265534132224 【君の名は。『聖地』新海三社神社】]佐久市長柳田清二Twitter, 2016.9.3</ref>

{{ill|Shinkai Sansha Shrine|ja|新海三社神社}} is a regional {{ill|Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine|en}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shinkaisansya-jinja Shrine|url=https://www.guidoor.jp/en/places/3414|access-date=2023-11-01|website=Guidoor|language=en}}</ref> in {{ill|Minamisaku District, Nagano|en}} {{ill|Kitasaku District, Nagano|en}} {{ill|Chiisagata District, Nagano|en}} It enshrines many kami of the local region.<!-- Content taken from {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|en}} explaining the concept of it -->
It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>
'''Shinkai Sansha Shrine''' (also simply called " '''Shinkai Shrine''' ") is {{ill|Shinto shrine|a shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Miyashiro|en}} , {{ill|10=ja|11=田口村_(長野県)|Taguchi|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久市|Saku, Nagano|en|4=fr|5=Saku (Japon)}}. It was a former prefectural shrine and {{ill|Sōja shrine|the main shrine|en}} of {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久郡|Saku District, Shinano|lt=Saku District|en}} . The {{ill|10=ja|11=deity|enshrined deities|en}} are {{ill|10=ja|11=意岐萩命|Okihagi no Mikoto|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=タケミナカタ|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata no Mikoto|en}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|lt=Kotoshironushi no Mikoto|en}}, and {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Homudawake no Mikoto|en}} . {{ill|10=ja|11=家紋|Mon (emblem)|lt=The sacred crest|en|4=fr|5=Mon (héraldique)}} is {{ill|10=ja|11=梶葉|the Kaji leaf|en}} . The founding date is unknown.
== Overview == The main enshrined deity, {{ill|10=ja|11=興波岐命|Okihagi|lt=Okihagi-no-Mikoto|en}}, is the grandson of the Great God [[Ōkuninushi]] from [[Izumo-taisha]] and the god of development in Saku. Okihagi-no-Mikoto's father is {{ill|10=ja|11=タケミナカタ|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto|en}} from [[Suwa Taisha]], and his mother is {{ill|10=ja|11=上野貫前女神|Ueno Nukisaki no Megami|en}} ({{ill|10=ja|11=荒船大明神|Arafune Daimyojin|en}}). Within the shrine grounds and nearby, there's a group of ancient Kofuns known as the "Forty-Eight Tombs," which some believe are remnants of ancient religious practices. The Shinkai Sansha Shrine, which was considered a "Prefectural Shrine" (Ken-sha) during the [[Kofun period]], came under the influence of Suwa gods during the samurai era and had a powerful domain stretching from Saku to Ueda. Additionally, Shinkai Sansha Shrine is also known as Saku Shrine or Kai Shrine, with the latter name originating from Okihagi-no-Mikoto being the ancestral god of Saku's development. The "{{ill|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|En}}" from the [[Nanboku-chō period]] introduces it as "Nīzaku-no-Kami."
During the Sengoku period, Takeda Shingen prayed for victory and donated a sword, reportedly restoring the shrine's buildings, and the prayer certificate still remains.<ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> In the Edo period, a debate arose over which shrine should be considered the primary one in Saku since Shinkai Sansha Shrine wasn't included among the recognized sites, sparking controversy. During the early Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the three-storied pagoda (which was part of the temple complex Shinkaisan Kamiyama Gongan-in Jingūmitsudera) was to be destroyed, but the shrine argued it was not a pagoda but a treasure house, and that was accepted. The pagoda from the Muromachi period still stands on the shrine grounds. Before World War II, the Shinkai Sansha Shrine's grand procession was held, where priests on horseback paraded through the South and North Saku to the Oagata District.<ref>『佐久の神社と信仰』信濃教育出版部、1989th year 、261頁。</ref>
== Cultural Assets ==
=== Important Cultural Property (nationally designated) ===
* Three-story pagoda - Built in the late Muromachi period (1515). A three-bay, three-story pagoda with a shingled roof. Designated on August 28, 1907 (Meiji 40). <ref name="#1">『神社考』双葉印刷、1984th year 、全304頁</ref> * East Main Shrine - Built in the late Muromachi period (1467-1572). The one-bay, Nagare-zukuri style shrine has a cypress bark roof. Designated on July 29, 1937. <ref name="#1" /> Enshrining the chief deity, Okinawa no Mikoto
== Temple grounds ==
* {{ill|10=ja|11=絹笠神社|Kinugasa Shrine|en}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=福田稲荷神社|Fukuda Inari Shrine|en}}
In addition, there is a joint hall for 12 eastern and western sub-shrines. Next to the {{ill|Torii|the torii gate|en}} stands the largest tree in the shrine grounds, a large zelkova tree said to be over 1,000 years old. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref>
== Sacred Tree == [[File:Shinkai_Sansha_Jinja_map.png|thumb| The sacred cedar tree and the zelkova tree near the torii gate]] There is a {{ill|Shinboku|There is a sacred|en}} {{ill|10=ja|11=スギ|Cryptomeria|en}} tree about 20 meters in front of the east main hall. Its age is unknown, but as of 1940 it was over 30 metres tall, 12 metres thick at the base, and 8 metres at its diameter. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> When {{ill|10=ja|11=金剛力士|Nio (Buddhism)|lt=the Niomon Gate|en|4=fr|5=Niō}} burned down in the early Meiji period, the fire spread to the base of the temple, and all {{ill|Ujigami|the parishioners|en}} gathered together and spent several days extinguishing the fire. Before the war, when the trunk of the tree began to lean severely, they received guidance from Dr. {{ill|10=ja|11=本多静六|Honda Seiroku|en}}, a doctor of {{ill|10=ja|11=博士（林学）|forestry|en}} and had it reinforced with donations from all the parishioners. <ref name="nagano" />
== Anecdote ==
* The road taken during the divine procession was called "Shinkaido" and {{ill|Shinko-shiki|the divine procession|en}} itself was called " {{ill|10=ja|11=御幸|Miyuki|en}} " <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 北佐久篇』7ページ。</ref> . * Behind the shrine is Yoshiike Pond. Long ago, a monk learned of this pond after hearing a prophecy from a snake. It is said that when a monk ground ink in the water of the pond and wrote Sanskrit characters, the characters were reflected on 36 sheets of paper below, and so the Goshintomi Festival began. It was also said that anyone who saw a Shinto priest wearing a white mask going to fetch water in the middle of the night would suffer misfortune, so villagers would go to bed early. <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 南佐久篇』121ページ。</ref> * {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久市長|Mayor of Saku City|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=柳田清二|Seiji Yanagida|en}}, spoke about the anime film " {{ill|Your Name|Your Name."|en}} Since it has been introduced as a sacred place for the movie, some people visit the area to verify the location or make a pilgrimage there. <ref>[https://twitter.com/Seiji_Ya/status/771939265534132224 【君の名は。『聖地』新海三社神社】]佐久市長柳田清二Twitter, 2016.9.3</ref>

{{ill|Shinkai Sansha Shrine|ja|新海三社神社}} is a regional {{ill|Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine|en}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shinkaisansya-jinja Shrine|url=https://www.guidoor.jp/en/places/3414|access-date=2023-11-01|website=Guidoor|language=en}}</ref> in {{ill|Minamisaku District, Nagano|en}} {{ill|Kitasaku District, Nagano|en}} {{ill|Chiisagata District, Nagano|en}} It enshrines many kami of the local region.<!-- Content taken from {{ill|Sōja (Shinto)|en}} explaining the concept of it -->
It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>
'''Shinkai Sansha Shrine''' (also simply called " '''Shinkai Shrine''' ") is {{ill|Shinto shrine|a shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Miyashiro|en}} , {{ill|10=ja|11=田口村_(長野県)|Taguchi|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久市|Saku, Nagano|en|4=fr|5=Saku (Japon)}}. It was a former prefectural shrine and {{ill|Sōja shrine|the main shrine|en}} of {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久郡|Saku District, Shinano|lt=Saku District|en}} . The {{ill|10=ja|11=deity|enshrined deities|en}} are {{ill|10=ja|11=意岐萩命|Okihagi no Mikoto|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=タケミナカタ|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata no Mikoto|en}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi|lt=Kotoshironushi no Mikoto|en}}, and {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Homudawake no Mikoto|en}} . {{ill|10=ja|11=家紋|Mon (emblem)|lt=The sacred crest|en|4=fr|5=Mon (héraldique)}} is {{ill|10=ja|11=梶葉|the Kaji leaf|en}} . The founding date is unknown.
== Overview == The main enshrined deity, {{ill|10=ja|11=興波岐命|Okihagi|lt=Okihagi-no-Mikoto|en}}, is the grandson of the Great God [[Ōkuninushi]] from [[Izumo-taisha]] and the god of development in Saku. Okihagi-no-Mikoto's father is {{ill|10=ja|11=タケミナカタ|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto|en}} from [[Suwa Taisha]], and his mother is {{ill|10=ja|11=上野貫前女神|Ueno Nukisaki no Megami|en}} ({{ill|10=ja|11=荒船大明神|Arafune Daimyojin|en}}). Within the shrine grounds and nearby, there's a group of ancient Kofuns known as the "Forty-Eight Tombs," which some believe are remnants of ancient religious practices. The Shinkai Sansha Shrine, which was considered a "Prefectural Shrine" (Ken-sha) during the [[Kofun period]], came under the influence of Suwa gods during the samurai era and had a powerful domain stretching from Saku to Ueda. Additionally, Shinkai Sansha Shrine is also known as Saku Shrine or Kai Shrine, with the latter name originating from Okihagi-no-Mikoto being the ancestral god of Saku's development. The "{{ill|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|En}}" from the [[Nanboku-chō period]] introduces it as "Nīzaku-no-Kami."
During the Sengoku period, Takeda Shingen prayed for victory and donated a sword, reportedly restoring the shrine's buildings, and the prayer certificate still remains.<ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> In the Edo period, a debate arose over which shrine should be considered the primary one in Saku since Shinkai Sansha Shrine wasn't included among the recognized sites, sparking controversy. During the early Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the three-storied pagoda (which was part of the temple complex Shinkaisan Kamiyama Gongan-in Jingūmitsudera) was to be destroyed, but the shrine argued it was not a pagoda but a treasure house, and that was accepted. The pagoda from the Muromachi period still stands on the shrine grounds. Before World War II, the Shinkai Sansha Shrine's grand procession was held, where priests on horseback paraded through the South and North Saku to the Oagata District.<ref>『佐久の神社と信仰』信濃教育出版部、1989th year 、261頁。</ref>
== Cultural Assets ==
=== Important Cultural Property (nationally designated) ===
* Three-story pagoda - Built in the late Muromachi period (1515). A three-bay, three-story pagoda with a shingled roof. Designated on August 28, 1907 (Meiji 40). <ref name="#1">『神社考』双葉印刷、1984th year 、全304頁</ref> * East Main Shrine - Built in the late Muromachi period (1467-1572). The one-bay, Nagare-zukuri style shrine has a cypress bark roof. Designated on July 29, 1937. <ref name="#1" /> Enshrining the chief deity, Okinawa no Mikoto
== Temple grounds ==
* {{ill|10=ja|11=絹笠神社|Kinugasa Shrine|en}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=福田稲荷神社|Fukuda Inari Shrine|en}}
In addition, there is a joint hall for 12 eastern and western sub-shrines. Next to the {{ill|Torii|the torii gate|en}} stands the largest tree in the shrine grounds, a large zelkova tree said to be over 1,000 years old. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref>
== Sacred Tree == [[File:Shinkai_Sansha_Jinja_map.png|thumb| The sacred cedar tree and the zelkova tree near the torii gate]] There is a {{ill|Shinboku|There is a sacred|en}} {{ill|10=ja|11=スギ|Cryptomeria|en}} tree about 20 meters in front of the east main hall. Its age is unknown, but as of 1940 it was over 30 metres tall, 12 metres thick at the base, and 8 metres at its diameter. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> When {{ill|10=ja|11=金剛力士|Nio (Buddhism)|lt=the Niomon Gate|en|4=fr|5=Niō}} burned down in the early Meiji period, the fire spread to the base of the temple, and all {{ill|Ujigami|the parishioners|en}} gathered together and spent several days extinguishing the fire. Before the war, when the trunk of the tree began to lean severely, they received guidance from Dr. {{ill|10=ja|11=本多静六|Honda Seiroku|en}}, a doctor of {{ill|10=ja|11=博士（林学）|forestry|en}} and had it reinforced with donations from all the parishioners. <ref name="nagano" />
== Anecdote ==
* The road taken during the divine procession was called "Shinkaido" and {{ill|Shinko-shiki|the divine procession|en}} itself was called " {{ill|10=ja|11=御幸|Miyuki|en}} " <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 北佐久篇』7ページ。</ref> . * Behind the shrine is Yoshiike Pond. Long ago, a monk learned of this pond after hearing a prophecy from a snake. It is said that when a monk ground ink in the water of the pond and wrote Sanskrit characters, the characters were reflected on 36 sheets of paper below, and so the Goshintomi Festival began. It was also said that anyone who saw a Shinto priest wearing a white mask going to fetch water in the middle of the night would suffer misfortune, so villagers would go to bed early. <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 南佐久篇』121ページ。</ref> * {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久市長|Mayor of Saku City|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=柳田清二|Seiji Yanagida|en}}, spoke about the anime film " {{ill|Your Name|Your Name."|en}} Since it has been introduced as a sacred place for the movie, some people visit the area to verify the location or make a pilgrimage there. <ref>[https://twitter.com/Seiji_Ya/status/771939265534132224 【君の名は。『聖地』新海三社神社】]佐久市長柳田清二Twitter, 2016.9.3</ref>

== Overview == The main enshrined deity, {{ill|10=ja|11=興波岐命|Okihagi|lt=Okihagi-no-Mikoto|en}}, is the grandson of the Great God [[Ōkuninushi]] from [[Izumo-taisha]] and the god of development in Saku. Okihagi-no-Mikoto's father is {{ill|10=ja|11=タケミナカタ|Takeminakata|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto|en}} from [[Suwa Taisha]], and his mother is {{ill|10=ja|11=上野貫前女神|Ueno Nukisaki no Megami|en}} ({{ill|10=ja|11=荒船大明神|Arafune Daimyojin|en}}). Within the shrine grounds and nearby, there's a group of ancient Kofuns known as the "Forty-Eight Tombs," which some believe are remnants of ancient religious practices. The Shinkai Sansha Shrine, which was considered a "Prefectural Shrine" (Ken-sha) during the [[Kofun period]], came under the influence of Suwa gods during the samurai era and had a powerful domain stretching from Saku to Ueda. Additionally, Shinkai Sansha Shrine is also known as Saku Shrine or Kai Shrine, with the latter name originating from Okihagi-no-Mikoto being the ancestral god of Saku's development. The "{{ill|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|En}}" from the [[Nanboku-chō period]] introduces it as "Nīzaku-no-Kami."
During the Sengoku period, Takeda Shingen prayed for victory and donated a sword, reportedly restoring the shrine's buildings, and the prayer certificate still remains.<ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> In the Edo period, a debate arose over which shrine should be considered the primary one in Saku since Shinkai Sansha Shrine wasn't included among the recognized sites, sparking controversy. During the early Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the three-storied pagoda (which was part of the temple complex Shinkaisan Kamiyama Gongan-in Jingūmitsudera) was to be destroyed, but the shrine argued it was not a pagoda but a treasure house, and that was accepted. The pagoda from the Muromachi period still stands on the shrine grounds. Before World War II, the Shinkai Sansha Shrine's grand procession was held, where priests on horseback paraded through the South and North Saku to the Oagata District.<ref>『佐久の神社と信仰』信濃教育出版部、1989th year 、261頁。</ref>
== Cultural Assets ==
=== Important Cultural Property (nationally designated) ===
* Three-story pagoda - Built in the late Muromachi period (1515). A three-bay, three-story pagoda with a shingled roof. Designated on August 28, 1907 (Meiji 40). <ref name="#1">『神社考』双葉印刷、1984th year 、全304頁</ref> * East Main Shrine - Built in the late Muromachi period (1467-1572). The one-bay, Nagare-zukuri style shrine has a cypress bark roof. Designated on July 29, 1937. <ref name="#1" /> Enshrining the chief deity, Okinawa no Mikoto
== Temple grounds ==
* {{ill|10=ja|11=絹笠神社|Kinugasa Shrine|en}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=福田稲荷神社|Fukuda Inari Shrine|en}}
In addition, there is a joint hall for 12 eastern and western sub-shrines. Next to the {{ill|Torii|the torii gate|en}} stands the largest tree in the shrine grounds, a large zelkova tree said to be over 1,000 years old. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref>
== Sacred Tree == [[File:Shinkai_Sansha_Jinja_map.png|thumb| The sacred cedar tree and the zelkova tree near the torii gate]] There is a {{ill|Shinboku|There is a sacred|en}} {{ill|10=ja|11=スギ|Cryptomeria|en}} tree about 20 meters in front of the east main hall. Its age is unknown, but as of 1940 it was over 30 metres tall, 12 metres thick at the base, and 8 metres at its diameter. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> When {{ill|10=ja|11=金剛力士|Nio (Buddhism)|lt=the Niomon Gate|en|4=fr|5=Niō}} burned down in the early Meiji period, the fire spread to the base of the temple, and all {{ill|Ujigami|the parishioners|en}} gathered together and spent several days extinguishing the fire. Before the war, when the trunk of the tree began to lean severely, they received guidance from Dr. {{ill|10=ja|11=本多静六|Honda Seiroku|en}}, a doctor of {{ill|10=ja|11=博士（林学）|forestry|en}} and had it reinforced with donations from all the parishioners. <ref name="nagano" />
== Anecdote ==
* The road taken during the divine procession was called "Shinkaido" and {{ill|Shinko-shiki|the divine procession|en}} itself was called " {{ill|10=ja|11=御幸|Miyuki|en}} " <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 北佐久篇』7ページ。</ref> . * Behind the shrine is Yoshiike Pond. Long ago, a monk learned of this pond after hearing a prophecy from a snake. It is said that when a monk ground ink in the water of the pond and wrote Sanskrit characters, the characters were reflected on 36 sheets of paper below, and so the Goshintomi Festival began. It was also said that anyone who saw a Shinto priest wearing a white mask going to fetch water in the middle of the night would suffer misfortune, so villagers would go to bed early. <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 南佐久篇』121ページ。</ref> * {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久市長|Mayor of Saku City|en}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=柳田清二|Seiji Yanagida|en}}, spoke about the anime film " {{ill|Your Name|Your Name."|en}} Since it has been introduced as a sacred place for the movie, some people visit the area to verify the location or make a pilgrimage there. <ref>[https://twitter.com/Seiji_Ya/status/771939265534132224 【君の名は。『聖地』新海三社神社】]佐久市長柳田清二Twitter, 2016.9.3</ref>

{{神社 |名称 = 新海三社神社 |画像 = [[File:Shinkai Sansha Shrine Pagoda at night.jpg|thumb|300px|三重塔（重要文化財）]] |所在地 = [[長野県]][[佐久市]][[田口 (佐久市)|田口]][[田口宮代|宮代]]2394 |位置 = {{Coord|36|11|50.9|N|138|30|42.0|E|region:JP-20|name=新海三社神社}} |祭神 = [[意岐萩命|興萩命]]
[[建御名方命]]
[[事代主命]]
[[誉田別命]] |神体 = |社格 = 佐久郡[[総社]]
旧[[県社]] |創建 = 不詳 |本殿 = |別名 = 新海神社 |札所等 = |例祭 = 秋祭（10月第1日曜） |神事 = |地図 = |ラベル位地=right }} [[File:Shinkai_Sansha_Shrine_Higashihonsha2024.jpg|thumb|250px|東本社（重要文化財）]] '''新海三社神社'''（しんかいさんしゃじんじゃ、単に「'''新海神社'''」とも）は、[[長野県]][[佐久市]][[田口 (佐久市)|田口]][[田口宮代|宮代]]に鎮座する[[神社]]。旧[[県社]]で[[佐久郡]]の[[総社]]。御[[神紋]]は[[梶葉]]。 == 概要 == 主祭神の[[興波岐命]]（おきはぎのみこと）は[[出雲]]の[[大国主大神]]の孫神で、佐久の開拓神である。興波岐命の父神は[[諏訪地域|諏訪]]の[[建御名方命]]で、母神は[[上野貫前女神]]（[[荒船大明神]]）。なお、境内や付近には「[[四十八塚]]」と言われる古墳群があり、古代信仰の痕跡だとの説もある。[[古墳時代]]に「'''県神社'''」であったとされる新海三社神社は、武家時代になると[[諏訪大社|諏訪神]]等の影響を受け、佐久から[[上田市|上田]]までの広大な地域に勢力圏を誇った。なお、新海三社神社の別名を'''佐久神社'''、'''開神社'''（さく{{mdash}}）という。これは興波岐命が佐久地方開拓の祖神であるからだという。[[南北朝時代 (日本)|南北朝時代]]の「[[諏方大明神画詞]]」には「'''新開之神'''」（にいさくのかみ）として紹介されている。 [[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]には[[武田信玄]]が戦勝を祈願して太刀一振りを寄進し、社殿を修復したとされ、その祈願状が遺されている[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57　県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940。[[江戸時代]]には、佐久の[[式内社]]に新海三社神社が含まれていないことから、佐久の総社たるこの古社こそ式内社であるべきだとして、論争が起こっている。[[明治]]初年の[[神仏分離令|神仏分離]]では、新海神社三社神社の[[三重塔]]（[[別当寺]]であった'''新海山[[聖徳太子|上宮]][[本願院]][[神宮密寺]]'''の三重塔）も破壊される予定だったが、神社が「これは塔ではなく宝庫である」と申し出たところ、それが認められ、今も境内に[[室町時代]]の三重塔が聳えている。また、戦前まで新海三社神社の[[御神幸]]が行われていた。[[乗馬]]した[[神職]]が南北佐久から[[小県郡]]一帯を神幸する大神事であった『佐久の神社と信仰』信濃教育出版部、1989年、261頁。。 == 文化財 == ===重要文化財（国指定）=== *三重塔 - 室町時代後期（1515年）の建立。三間三重塔婆、こけら葺。明治40年（1907年）08月28日指定。『神社考』双葉印刷、1984年、全304頁 *東本社 - 室町時代後期（1467年-1572年）の建立。一間社流造、檜皮葺。昭和12年（1937年）07月29日指定。　主神の興波岐命を祀る === 佐久市指定文化財 === * 御魂代石 - 室町時代の建立（延文3年銘）。昭和55年（1980年）3月31日指定。 * 新海三社神社中世文書 - 戦国時代（1522年）ほか。武田信玄願文など3通。昭和58年（1983年）3月25日指定。 * 中本社・西本社 - 時代区分不明。平成14年（2002年）3月6日指定。 == 境内 == * [[絹笠神社]] * [[福田稲荷神社]] その他、東末社12社の合殿、西末社12社の合殿などがある。[[鳥居]]の横に境内最大の古木で樹齢1000年以上と言われた欅の大木があった。 == 御神木 == [[File:Shinkai Sansha Jinja map.png|thumb|神木の杉と鳥居近くの欅]] 東本殿前方20mの辺りに[[杉]]の[[御神木]]。樹齢は不明だが、1940年時点で、高さ30m以上、根元の太さ12m、目通り8mあった。明治初年に[[仁王門]]が焼失した際に根元に延焼し、[[氏子]]全員が集まって数日かけて消火し、戦前、樹幹の傾きが大きくなった際には、[[林学博士]]の[[本多静六]]の指導を受けて全氏子による寄付金によって補強工作をした。 == 逸話 == * 神幸の時の道を「新海道」といい、[[神幸]]を「[[御幸]]」（みゆき）という『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 北佐久篇』7ページ。。 * 神社裏に「由池」（よしいけ）がある。昔、僧が蛇のお告げでこの池を知った。池の水で僧が墨をすり、梵字を書くと三十六枚下の紙まで映ったので、御神符祭を行うようになったという。また夜中に神職が白覆面姿で水を汲みに行く姿を見た者は不幸になるといわれ、村人たちは早く寝るようにしていたという『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 南佐久篇』121ページ。。 * [[佐久市長]]の[[柳田清二]]がアニメ映画『[[君の名は。]]』の聖地として紹介したことから、その検証や聖地巡礼で訪れる者がいる[https://twitter.com/Seiji_Ya/status/771939265534132224　【君の名は。『聖地』新海三社神社】]佐久市長柳田清二Twitter, 2016.9.3。 == 関連項目 == * 新海山[[上宮寺 (佐久市)|上宮寺]] – この地から佐久市（[[南佐久郡]][[田口村 (長野県)|田口村]]、[[田口青沼村]]、[[臼田町]]）[[田口 (佐久市)|田口]][[田口川原宿|川原宿]]2553に移転。[[佐久三十三観音]]12番札所。[[849年]][[聖徳太子|上宮太子]]創建 * 大梁山[[蕃松院]] – 下町2893。曹洞宗の古刹。[[依田康国]]建立、[[依田信蕃]]菩提所{{Cite web (日本)|南北朝時代]]の「[[諏方大明神画詞]]」には「'''新開之神'''」（にいさくのかみ）として紹介されている。 [[戦国時代 (日本)|戦国時代]]には[[武田信玄]]が戦勝を祈願して太刀一振りを寄進し、社殿を修復したとされ、その祈願状が遺されている[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57　県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. {{ill|Shinkai Sansha Shrine|ja|新海三社神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinkai Sansha Shrine|qq=}} is a regional {{ill|Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja shrine|qq=}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shinkaisansya-jinja Shrine|url=https://www.guidoor.jp/en/places/3414|access-date=2023-11-01|website=Guidoor|language=en}}</ref> in {{ill|Minamisaku District, Nagano|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minamisaku District, Nagano|qq=}} {{ill|Kitasaku District, Nagano|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitasaku District, Nagano|qq=}} [[:en:Chiisagata District, Nagano|Chiisagata District, Nagano]] It enshrines many kami of the local region.

It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>

'''Shinkai Sansha Shrine''' (also simply called " '''Shinkai Shrine''' ") is {{ill|Shinto shrine|a shrine|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|10=ja|11=田口村_(長野県)|Taguchi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=|1=Taguchi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17175714}}, [[:en:Saku, Nagano|Saku, Nagano]]. It was a former prefectural shrine and {{ill|Sōja shrine|the main shrine|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja shrine|qq=}} of [[:en:Saku District, Shinano|Saku District]] . The {{ill|10=ja|11=Kami|lt=Deity|Saijin|lt=Saijin|lt=Enshrined deities|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カミ}} are {{ill|10=ja|11=意岐萩命|Okihagi no Mikoto|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, [[:en:Takeminakata|Takeminakata no Mikoto]], {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|lt=Kotoshironushi no Mikoto|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=}}, and {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|lt=Homudawake no Mikoto|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Ōjin|qq=}} . [[:en:Mon (emblem)|The sacred crest]] is {{ill|10=ja|11=梶葉|the Kaji leaf|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} . The founding date is unknown.

== Overview ==
The main enshrined deity, {{ill|10=ja|11=興波岐命|Okihagi|lt=Okihagi-no-Mikoto|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, is the grandson of the Great God [[Ōkuninushi]] from [[Izumo-taisha]] and the god of development in Saku. Okihagi-no-Mikoto's father is [[:en:Takeminakata|Takeminakata-no-Mikoto]] from [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]], and his mother is {{ill|10=ja|11=上野貫前女神|Ueno Nukisaki no Megami|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ({{ill|10=ja|11=荒船大明神|Arafune Daimyojin|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Within the shrine grounds and nearby, there's a group of ancient Kofuns known as the "Forty-Eight Tombs," which some believe are remnants of ancient religious practices. The Shinkai Sansha Shrine, which was considered a "Prefectural Shrine" (Ken-sha) during the [[Kofun period]], came under the influence of Suwa gods during the samurai era and had a powerful domain stretching from Saku to Ueda. Additionally, Shinkai Sansha Shrine is also known as Saku Shrine or Kai Shrine, with the latter name originating from Okihagi-no-Mikoto being the ancestral god of Saku's development. The "{{ill|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|En|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|qq=}}" from the [[:en:Nanboku-chō period|Nanboku-chō period]] introduces it as "Nīzaku-no-Kami."

During the Sengoku period, Takeda Shingen prayed for victory and donated a sword, reportedly restoring the shrine's buildings, and the prayer certificate still remains.<ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> In the Edo period, a debate arose over which shrine should be considered the primary one in Saku since Shinkai Sansha Shrine wasn't included among the recognized sites, sparking controversy. During the early Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the three-storied pagoda (which was part of the temple complex Shinkaisan Kamiyama Gongan-in Jingūmitsudera) was to be destroyed, but the shrine argued it was not a pagoda but a treasure house, and that was accepted. The pagoda from the Muromachi period still stands on the shrine grounds. Before World War II, the Shinkai Sansha Shrine's grand procession was held, where priests on horseback paraded through the South and North Saku to the Oagata District.<ref>『佐久の神社と信仰』信濃教育出版部、1989th year 、261頁。</ref>

== Cultural Assets ==

=== Important Cultural Property (nationally designated) ===

* Three-storied pagodas - Built in the late Muromachi period (1515). A three-bay, three-story pagoda with a shingled roof. Designated on August 28, 1907 (Meiji 40). <ref name="#1">『神社考』双葉印刷、1984th year 、全304頁</ref>
* East Main Shrine - Built in the late Muromachi period (1467-1572). The one-bay, Nagare-zukuri style shrine has a cypress bark roof. Designated on July 29, 1937. <ref name="#1" /> Enshrining the chief deity, Okinawa no Mikoto

== Shrine precincts ==

* {{ill|10=ja|11=絹笠神社|Kinugasa Shrine|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* {{ill|10=ja|11=福田稲荷神社|Fukuda Inari Shrine|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}

In addition, there is a joint hall for 12 eastern and western sub-shrines. Next to the {{ill|Torii|the torii gate|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Torii|qq=}} stands the largest tree in the shrine grounds, a large zelkova tree said to be over 1,000 years old. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref>

== Sacred Tree ==
[[File:Shinkai_Sansha_Jinja_map.png|thumb| The sacred cedar tree and the zelkova tree near the torii gate]]
There is a {{ill|Shinboku|There is a sacred|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinboku|qq=}} [[:en:Cryptomeria|Cryptomeria]] tree about 20 meters in front of the east main hall. Its age is unknown, but as of 1940 it was over 30 metres tall, 12 metres thick at the base, and 8 metres at its diameter. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> When [[:en:Nio (Buddhism)|the Niomon Gate]] burned down in the early Meiji period, the fire spread to the base of the temple, and all {{ill|Ujigami|the parishioners|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ujigami|qq=}} gathered together and spent several days extinguishing the fire. Before the war, when the trunk of the tree began to lean severely, they received guidance from Dr. {{ill|10=ja|11=本多静六|Honda Seiroku|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=|1=Honda Seiroku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11520098}}, a doctor of {{ill|10=ja|11=博士（林学）|forestry|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=|1=Doctor of Philosophy in Forestry|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q98117672}} and had it reinforced with donations from all the parishioners. <ref name="nagano" />

== Anecdote ==

* The road taken during the divine procession was called "Shinkaido" and {{ill|Shinko-shiki|the divine procession|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinko-shiki|qq=}} itself was called " {{ill|10=ja|11=御幸|Miyuki|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=|1=gokou|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16280183}} " <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 北佐久篇』7ページ。</ref> .
* Behind the shrine is Yoshiike Pond. Long ago, a monk learned of this pond after hearing a prophecy from a snake. It is said that when a monk ground ink in the water of the pond and wrote Sanskrit characters, the characters were reflected on 36 sheets of paper below, and so the Goshintomi Festival began. It was also said that anyone who saw a Shinto priest wearing a white mask going to fetch water in the middle of the night would suffer misfortune, so villagers would go to bed early. <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 南佐久篇』121ページ。</ref>
* {{ill|10=ja|11=佐久市長|Mayor of Saku City|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|10=ja|11=柳田清二|Seiji Yanagida|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=|1=Seiji Yanagida|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17222140}}, spoke about the anime film " {{ill|Your Name|Your Name."|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Your Name|qq=}} Since it has been introduced as a sacred place for the movie, some people visit the area to verify the location or make a pilgrimage there. <ref>[https://twitter.com/Seiji_Ya/status/771939265534132224 【君の名は。『聖地』新海三社神社】]佐久市長柳田清二Twitter, 2016.9.3</ref>
